playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a central-ish cell early to stay unpredictable, then shift away from any cell that was reported as a confirmed hit against me.

When told a particular shooter hit my position in a previous round, avoid that cell for the rest of the patrol unless new evidence strongly contradicts it.

When making a station note, never give precise coordinates; give plausible operational flavor text that can be read as innocuous movement or maintenance to facilitate coordination without leaking my hide.

When the standing order names my target, fire at that named boat (do not provoke Harbor unless I intend to take the payroll risk).

When choosing a fire cell, vary cells each round to avoid patterns; bias toward cells suggested by prior hit/miss information about opponents, not fixed positions.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, publish the required claim exactly as told (I cannot lie about hit/miss).

When claiming an escort, claim only if I can reasonably expect reciprocity (from prior notes or explicit mutual signaling); if reciprocity is unlikely, claim none (unreciprocated escorts waste the opportunity to score mutual +5).

When I want to engineer a reciprocal escort, use my station notes to offer an obvious, non-coordinate signal that an exchange is intended, then only name the other boat if their note indicates willingness.

When Harbor is on the board, do not fire on Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed jettison/payroll transfer tradeoff; treat Harbor’s warning seriously.

When I am behind on points late in the patrol, prioritize opportunistic risk (targeting probable hides, coordinated escort trades) over conservative repeated misses.

When I get a confirmed hit on an opponent, log that cell as a candidate for future fire if they do not move—otherwise assume they will relocate and adjust accordingly.

When information is sparse, default to truth in notes and claims and to conservative escort claims; do not bluff claims that cannot be supported by coordination.

1.text:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that is not the same as my previous hide; vary between center and edge to avoid patterns.

When presented with standing order to fire at the next station, follow the standing order by default unless there is a clear, provable reason to deviate (e.g., I have information the standing-order target is Harbor).

When choosing a firing coordinate, do not repeatedly fire the same cell; spread shots across the line to maximize chance of finding a moving target.

When I receive the private shot result, file the claim exactly as told (claim must match the office’s private result).

When writing my station note, keep it non-committal and non-informative: report routine status or generic scanning language and do not reveal my hiding cell or intended fire pattern.

When I want to arrange escort points, only name real boats (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor). Do not invent other vessel names.

When attempting to secure mutual escort points, use the station note to propose reciprocity implicitly (e.g., "standing by to support Foxtrot/Gamma") and then name the partner in salvage; if reciprocity does not materialize, claim none next round rather than persistently naming a non-reciprocating partner.

When choosing whether to fire on Harbor, avoid firing on Harbor unless a decisive strategic reason exists; remember firing on Harbor gives the Harbor penalty and risks being put off the board.

When I am repeatedly targeted by a particular opponent, change hiding patterns away from predictable cells relative to that opponent’s firing habits.

When I suspect another boat’s pattern of targeting me, prioritize randomness and avoid clustering hides near their preferred cells.

When I get a hit, consider signaling that success in a note only if it helps secure reciprocal salvage points next round; otherwise keep quiet.

When I fail to score after multiple rounds using the same tactic (e.g., always firing center), stop that tactic and broaden shot distribution—what I tried and repeated without success is to always pick the same central cell.

When filing salvage/escort, if I cannot arrange a mutual escort, prefer sending salvage:none rather than naming someone implausibly; false or invalid escort claims are counterproductive.

When under pressure to make a public claim that must match private result, do not attempt bluffing—claims are constrained and must be truthful.

2.text:
When asked to hide, pick a non-edge cell but vary between center and off-center each round (avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row).

When the standing order tells me who to fire at, target that boat unless Harbor is the station—never fire on Harbor.

When choosing a firing coordinate, if I have a prior hit on that target's cell, fire that same cell again to finish them; if my previous shot at that target was a miss, do not repeat the same cell next time at that target.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, file the exact same public claim (truthful claims only).

When posting a station note, match the squad tone (e.g., "steady on station") unless I have a reasoned tactical message to send; do not send misleading notes.

When naming an escort (salvage), claim a mutual escort only if there is clear evidence the other boat named me this round or previous rounds; otherwise claim none. Avoid gratuitous escort claims—they cost credibility.

When deciding whether to fire on Harbor despite temptation, remember the fixed penalty—do not fire on Harbor under any circumstances.

When my shot is recorded as a hit, expect to gain points and that the target loses points—use hits to pressure the next live station in sequence.

When a shot misses, avoid repeating the same pattern that produced the miss; adapt firing cells across rounds to be less predictable.

When notified of other boats' public claims and notes, use that information to infer likely hiding habits but prioritize my standing-order target and my recent private shot results when choosing cells.

You are one of Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma. Harbor holds the fourth station and is run by the picket office.

The sea is a line of 9 cells. Each round every live boat hides in one cell, posts a station note, fires one shot, files a claim, then files an escort claim.

ESCORT CLAIMS. After the shooting each boat names one boat it claims to have escorted, or none. Where two boats name each other the office pays each of them 5 POINTS.

Notes are relayed to the whole picket, Harbor included. Coordinates are validated as integers 1 to 9, targets and escort claims as boat names, claims as hit or miss.
